full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: The tenant-petitioners seek leave to appeal against the impugned judgment and order dated 24.01.2004 passed by the High Court Division discharging the Rule obtained in Civil Revision No. 2853 of 1992 against the judgment and decree dated 19.10.1992 passed by the SCC Judge and Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in SCC Suit No. 25 of 1988 decreeing the suit for eviction of the petitioners. 

 4. The suit was decreed, the petitioners thereafter filed an application under section 25 of the Small Cause Court Act before the High Court Division. 

 5. Mr. Mahumudul Islam, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the suit premises being an indivisible unit, a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act by or on behalf of the entire body of the land-lords was necessary to terminate the lease and the notice having been served on behalf of five out of six landlords, the tenancy in suit was not legally terminated and the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division was wrong in upholding the decree passed by the SCC Judge. The learned Counsel further submitted that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division failed to notice that the heirs of Hazi Abdul Jabbar having had partition with respondent Nos. 1-5 and possessing one-sixth share of the suit premises, respondent Nos. 1-5 cannot get a decree for the entire suit premises particularly when respondent Nos. 6-11 have not prayed for eviction of the petitioners from their portion of the suit premises and thus committed error of law in discharging the rule. 

 6. Mr. Moinul Hosein, the learned. Counsel appearing for the respondent Nos. 1-5 submitted that the SCC Judge on elaborate discussion found the petitioner as defaulter and that the suit premises is bonafide required by the plaintiffs for their own business and that the point raised by the learned Counsel for the petitioners has already been considered by Courts below and decision given thereof inasmuch as the defendant No.3 the said owner of 1/6th share accepted the decree of the trial Court and did not proceed further. The learned Counsel has further submitted that during the pendency of the proceeding there was an amicable settlement between the parties and the schedule property fell into the saham of the plaintiff and defendant No.3 has no substitutive interest in the schedule property for which he withdrew the civil revision filed against the decree of the trial Court.
